newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 2.32 pct in recovery.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 2.32 pct in recovery.

text.p: Turkish shares firmed an average 2.32 percent in reaction buys on Wednesday, following Tuesday's 8.76 percent plunge caused by heavy profit-taking.
The IMKB National-100 gained 36 points, or 2.32 percent to close at 1,587, compared to Monday's all-time high close of 1,700. It brushed a low of 1,483 in early trade.
Trade volume plunged to 48.52 trillion lira ($419 million) from Monday's record high 71.85 trillion ($619.4 million).
"Selling pressure continued in early trade, but afterwards there was a technical rebound. I expect a rise until the weekend," said Ozturk Kayiran from Alternatifbank.

Brokers said sentiment soured a bit after Tuesday news that only two bids were received in the tender for the block sell-off of a 30-40 percent stake in largely state-owned flat steel maker and bluechip Eregli.

"The negative mood seems to have disappeared. The dowtrend in (money and bond) interest rates and quiet currency trade continues, leaving the stock market as the sole address for investments," said Orhan Kazici from Info securities.

The index had gained 74.2 percent, breaking 17 record closes from end-1996 to Monday's close. The rise was 61.5 percent in dollar terms. The rally had accelerated sharply after last Thursday's contitutional court ruling giving green light to Turk Telekom's sell-off.
